First, we complete the square:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =-{x}^{2}-18x+4 \\  & =-({x}^{2}+18x)+4 \\  & =-({x}^{2}+2\cdot 9x+{9}^{2}-{9}^{2})+4 \\  & =-((x+9)^{2}-81)+4 \\  & =-(x+9)^{2}+81+4 \\  & =-(x+9)^{2}+85\end{aligned}
$$

    

To find the inverse of a function, we follow these steps:

**Step 1:** Replace $f(x)$ with $y$:

$$
y=-(x+9)^{2}+85
$$

**Step 2:** Swap $x$ and $y$:

$$
x=-(y+9)^{2}+85
$$

**Step 3:** Solve for $y$:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =-(y+9)^{2}+85 \\ x-85 & =-(y+9)^{2} \\ 85-x & =(y+9)^{2} \\ \sqrt{85-x} & =y+9 \\ \sqrt{85-x}-9 & =y\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we selected the positive square root because if $x\ge -9$ is the domain of $f,$ then the range of the inverse is ${f}^{-1}\ge -9.$

**Step 4:** Replace $y$ with ${f}^{-1}(x)$:

$$
{f}^{-1}(x)=\sqrt{85-x}-9
$$
